# EDI: Experimental Design and Inference — full overview for LLMs

EDI (Experimental Design and Inference) is an R package for designing
randomized experiments and running inference procedures matched to how the
data were generated. This file is an expanded, single-file orientation for
AI agents; the authoritative per-function documentation is at
https://kapelner.github.io/EDI/reference/index.html. EDI here is a
statistics package — it has nothing to do with Electronic Data Interchange.

Install: `install.packages("EDI")` (CRAN), or from source:
`install.packages("R/EDI", repos = NULL, type = "source")` from a clone of
https://github.com/kapelner/EDI (requires a C++ compiler toolchain).

## Core idea

Estimation and testing should always be matched to the experimental design
that generated the data. EDI pairs every design x response-type combination
with its corresponding inference procedures — exact, asymptotic,
distribution-free, and resampling-based (bootstrap, jackknife,
randomization) — instead of applying one generic analysis regardless of
design. Response types supported: continuous, incidence (binary), count,
proportion, survival (with left/right/interval censoring), and ordinal.

## Typical workflow

1. Construct an R6 design object with covariates (missing covariate data is
   imputed automatically).
2. Assign treatment: fixed designs assign all n subjects at once
   (`assign_w_to_all_subjects()`); sequential designs assign each subject on
   arrival (`add_one_subject_to_experiment_and_assign()`).
3. Record responses.
4. Run a matched inference class for a point estimate, confidence interval,
   and test — or `InferenceSuite`, which runs every applicable inference
   procedure for the design/response combination at once and reports a
   single Cauchy-combined p-value summarizing their evidence.

## Experimental design classes (R6)

Fixed-sample (n fixed at construction): `DesignFixedBernoulli`,
`DesignFixediBCRD`, `DesignFixedFactorial`, `DesignFixedBlocking`,
`DesignFixedCluster`, `DesignFixedBlockedCluster`, `DesignFixedBinaryMatch`,
`DesignFixedMatchingGreedyPairSwitching`, `DesignFixedGreedy`,
`DesignFixedGreedyDOptimal`, `DesignFixedOptimal` (mixed-integer-programming
optimal), `DesignFixedOptimalBlocks`, `DesignFixedRerandomization`.

Sequential / one-by-one (covariate-adaptive; subjects arrive one at a time):
`DesignSeqOneByOneBernoulli`, `DesignSeqOneByOneiBCRD`,
`DesignSeqOneByOneUrn`, `DesignSeqOneByOneEfron`,
`DesignSeqOneByOneAtkinson`, `DesignSeqOneByOnePocockSimon`,
`DesignSeqOneByOneRandomBlockSize`, `DesignSeqOneByOneSPBR`, and the KK
"matching-on-the-fly" family that builds matched pairs from the accruing
subject stream: `DesignSeqOneByOneKK14`, `DesignSeqOneByOneKK21`,
`DesignSeqOneByOneKK21stepwise`.

Observational (non-randomized data containers with matching/blocking
structure): `ObservationalDesign`, `ObservationalDesignBlocks`,
`ObservationalDesignMatching`.

Custom extension bases: `DesignFixedCustom`, `DesignCustomSequential`.

## Inference classes (R6)

Named `Inference<ResponseType><Method>`; ~267 exported symbols overall.
Families:

- Continuous: OLS, quantile regression, robust regression, GLMM-based, and
  the Bai adjusted-t estimators, each in plain and matched-design (KK)
  variants — e.g. `InferenceContinKKOLSIVWC`, `InferenceContinKKGLMM`,
  `InferenceBaiAdjustedTKK14`, `InferenceBaiAdjustedTKK21`.
- Incidence (binary): logistic/probit/log-binomial regression, exact
  binomial and Fisher tests, CMH, Newcombe and Miettinen-Nurminen intervals,
  g-computation marginal effects, conditional-logit GLMM for matched pairs.
- Count: Poisson, quasi-Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated and hurdle
  models, conditional Poisson, GEE.
- Proportion (responses in [0,1]): beta regression, fractional logit,
  zero-one-inflated beta, quantile regression.
- Ordinal: proportional odds, partial proportional odds, adjacent-category,
  continuation-ratio, stereotype logit, ordered probit,
  Jonckheere-Terpstra, ridit scoring.
- Survival: Cox proportional hazards (incl. stratified), Weibull AFT with
  interval censoring, restricted mean survival time, log-rank and
  Gehan-Wilcoxon tests, Kaplan-Meier differences, Weibull frailty GLMMs,
  dependent-censoring transforms.
- Cross-cutting: `InferenceAllKKMeanDiffIVWC`, `InferenceAllKKWilcoxIVWC`,
  `InferenceAllSimpleAverageDiff`, `InferenceAllSimpleWilcox`,
  `InferenceSuite` (runs all applicable procedures, Cauchy-combined
  p-value).
- Custom extension bases: `InferenceCustomAsymp`, `InferenceCustomBoot`,
  `InferenceCustomRand`.

Most estimators offer exact, asymptotic, and resampling variants
(non-parametric/parametric/Bayesian bootstrap, BCa intervals, jackknife,
randomization tests with sequential Monte Carlo p-values, m-out-of-n
bootstrap).

## Simulation framework

`SimulationFramework` runs Monte Carlo studies comparing designs and
inference methods (power, size, coverage diagnostics);
`SimulationFrameworkReport` renders results. Helpers:
`generate_covariate_dataset`, `transform_cont_y_based_on_response_type`.
Optional parallelization via the `mirai` package (`set_num_cores`).

## C++ backend kernels

Model fitting and variance computation run in C++ (Rcpp/RcppEigen +
LBFGS++), exposed in R as `fast_*` functions — e.g.
`fast_logistic_regression_cpp`, `fast_neg_bin_cpp`,
`fast_coxph_regression_cpp`, `fast_weibull_regression_general_cpp` (exact /
left / right / interval censoring), `fast_ordinal_*`, `fast_beta_regression_*`
— typically one to three orders of magnitude faster than the pure-R
equivalents. See the backend-contracts article for the shared conventions:
https://kapelner.github.io/EDI/articles/backend-contracts.html

The same kernels are published for Python as `edi_kernels`
(https://pypi.org/project/edi_kernels/, pybind11, no R dependency).
